name: spellcast
description: SpellCast is a PROTOTYPE of a fully decentralized, peer-to-peer Twitter-like application that runs entirely in your web browser. Share messages (called "spells") directly with your connections without relying on any central servers.

paragraphs: Cast spells, not tweets. SpellCast is a Twitter-like social app with no servers, no sign-ups, and no company in the middle. Your messages (called "spells") travel directly between you and the people you connect with, and everything lives in your own browser. It's a single web page - nothing to install.

⚠️ SpellCast is an early prototype. It's a genuinely working, fun way to explore serverless social messaging - just don't rely on it for anything safety-critical yet. The honest details are in the technical notes.
Most social apps are free because you are the product. SpellCast takes the opposite approach:
features: No servers, no middleman. There's no company database holding your posts. Messages go peer-to-peer, straight between browsers - nothing central to hack, sell, or shut down.
No sign-up, ever. No email, no phone number, no password. You pick a username, get an ID, and you're in.
Your data stays with you. Posts, images, and contacts live in your browser - not in someone else's cloud.
Private by design. No ads, no tracking, no profiling. Connections are encrypted in transit (WebRTC/DTLS), and messages only travel to people in your own network.
Works everywhere. Any modern desktop or mobile browser - iPhone, iPad, Android, laptop. Connect with a friend in seconds by scanning a QR code.

requirements.text: Back up your key from Profile → Export Credential Backup (passphrase-encrypted) and restore it on another device from the login screen.

Your peer ID is still your network address and login for now; moving your credentials to another device is done via the encrypted credential backup — either the backup file, or Profile → Show Backup QR and Login → Scan Backup QR on the new device — rather than re-typing the ID.
You can self-host the broker + TURN to keep that off third-party servers.
